title: Lift gnocchi out of simmering water with a slotted spoon as they float up, then switch the heat off
instruction: The gnocchi are cooking; each is done when it floats up. Lift them out onto the plate with the slotted spoon as they are done, then put the spoon down and switch the heat off.
context: Gnocchi from a pack are a familiar meal to cook at home, and the rule on the pack is the one cooks go by: they are done when they float. The pieces go into simmering water together, sink and lie on the pan's floor for over a minute, then come up within seconds of one another. From then on the clock runs: they are soft, so they are lifted out with a slotted spoon, a few at a time, not poured through a strainer, and those left in the water turn sticky and crumbly. It is the job of taking dumplings or poached eggs out of a pot: read the cue in the water, work with a tool in a vessel, keep the pan where it stands, be done in time, and end by switching the heat off. The idea is that of the program's pull request #2048, whose review asked for "a realistic batch of gnocchi" in place of a staged two-at-a-time schedule "while retaining spoon-based retrieval"; scene, kit, numbers and text here are our own.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. A built-in 30 cm domino induction hob with two zones (sizes of Bosch PIB375FB1E: glass 306 mm wide and 527 mm deep, zones 21.0 and 14.5 cm), lying 6 mm proud of the bench, fixed, its front edge at x 12.75 on the midline; its on/off key (x 14.5, y 7.0) and red lamp (x 14.5, y 4.5) on the front strip. A stainless saute pan, 24 cm across and 7 cm deep inside, with 2.5 litres of plain tap water, 5.5 cm deep, held at a gentle simmer (95 C, give or take 3, by a kitchen thermometer; 4.0 kg with the water), standing loose on the front zone at x 30.5, y 0, its handle pointing away from the arms. Twelve potato gnocchi from a 500 g bag of De Cecco Gnocchi di Patate no. 401 (26 x 18 x 15 mm, 6 g each, 72 g: assumed, to be measured on the bought pack), tipped into the water together as the trial starts, on the pan's floor on the side of the pan away from the right arm, at places drawn from the seed. A 20 cm plate at x 32.5, y -26. A nylon slotted spoon with a cranked handle (334.5 mm, 60 g, bowl 90 x 69 mm and 15 mm deep) with its bowl on a spoon rest at x 71, y -37, handle towards the arms. By seed: when each piece floats up (between 80 and 90 s after the start, each on its own), where each lies and how it is turned.
scoring: A piece counts when it floated, left the water after that and no more than 90 s later, lies on the plate at rest, and was never touched by a gripper (a grasp point within 20 mm of its middle). 0 for the trial if the pan was pushed more than 3 cm from where it stood at any moment of the trial, or a piece that never floated lies on the plate (raw food served). 0.25: 3 pieces count. 0.5: 6. 0.75: 9, with the heat off and the spoon put down. 1.0: 11 of the 12, with the heat off and the spoon put down. While the heat is on or the spoon is in a gripper the score is never above 0.5. Several pieces to a spoonful are allowed. Real bench: the overhead trial video gives when each piece comes up and when it leaves the water, and the pan against the front zone's ring through the whole trial (a pan pushed more than 3 cm and put back still scores 0); the final photo confirms the end state: plate, spoon, lamp, pan. Tipping the pan is not scored: the arms cannot tip a 4 kg pan (shown by a run); its tilt is reported.
reset_notes: Gnocchi: De Cecco Gnocchi di Patate no. 401, 500 g bag, kept unopened as the pack directs (away from light and heat) until the session; the pieces are at room temperature (18 to 24 C) when used. The bag is opened just before the first trial and not kept for another day. Each trial: a fresh twelve, separated by hand, laid on a second plate and tipped into the water together on the side of the pan away from the right arm; the trial starts within 3 s of that. Before each trial: water topped up to 5.5 cm and back at a gentle simmer (95 C, give or take 3); pan centred on the front zone's ring; serving plate wiped; spoon on its rest with the handle towards the arms; heat on. Gripper pads sleeved against steam and splashes; nothing but the spoon goes into the water.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX. The water is not a fluid: each piece gets lift, drag and a drift; raw it lies on the floor, done it floats. Float times (80 to 90 s) and the 90 s rule are from a published kitchen test of the same product, not measured on our bench; the bobbing before the final float is not modeled. Nothing drains, splashes or is hot; the surface is drawn opaque. Pieces are rigid: a gripper touching one stands in for squashing it. Piece size, lift and drag are assumed. Details: README.
